topic: Instantaneous Rate of Change and the Derivative

outline.topic: Instantaneous Rate of Change and the Derivative

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Average Rate of Change
sections.content: Recall the slope formula (rise over run) applied to a secant line connecting two points on a curve. Emphasize that average rate provides a 'big picture' but misses the nuance of fluctuations.
sections.example: A cheetah runs 100 meters in 5 seconds. Its average speed is 20 m/s, but we know it accelerated and decelerated throughout the sprint.

sections.title: The Concept of 'Zooming In'
sections.content: Introduce the visual animation: Gradually move the second point closer to the first. As the interval (delta x) approaches zero, the secant line morphs into a tangent line touching only one point.
sections.example: Visualizing a drone flight path on a graph; as the time interval shrinks to a micro-second, the curve looks like a straight line representing the exact velocity at that blink of an eye.

sections.title: Formalizing the Derivative Definition
sections.content: Introduce the mathematical limit notation: f'(x) = lim (h→0) [f(x+h) - f(x)] / h. Explain that this limit is the bridge between average rate and instantaneous rate.
sections.example: Using a speedometer animation: The needle represents the derivative, constantly updating as 'h' (time slice) approaches zero.

sections.title: Application: Predicting Change
sections.content: Demonstrate how the derivative (slope of the tangent) tells us if a function is increasing, decreasing, or at a peak/valley at a precise instant.
sections.example: A smart-grow plant sensor: The derivative tells the gardener exactly how fast the plant is growing at 2:00 PM, allowing for precise nutrient adjustment.

sections.title: Summary and Conclusion
sections.content: Recap: Derivative = Instantaneous Rate = Slope of the Tangent Line. Encourage viewing Calculus as the mathematics of 'now'.
sections.example: Reviewing the cheetah's run: Instead of just 'average speed', we can now describe its exact velocity at the 2.5-second mark.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite: The Average Rate of Change
lecture_lines: Average speed is total distance over total time.
Secant lines show average slope between two points.
But cheetahs change speed throughout the sprint.
animations: Display two points on a curve, connect them with a secant line in #FFD700 (Gold).
Animate the secant line shifting as the second point approaches the first.
Highlight the slope calculation formula: m = Δy/Δx in #FFFFFF (White).
Show the Δx term shrinking towards zero visually.
Label the secant line as 'Average Rate of Change' in #87CEEB (SkyBlue).

storyboard.title: The Concept of 'Zooming In'
lecture_lines: What if the two points get closer?
The secant line tilts as we zoom in.
It eventually looks like a single point.
animations: Start with a zoomed-out view of a smooth curve.
Focus the camera on a small segment to reveal local linearity.
Draw a tangent line touching the curve at one point in #FF4500 (OrangeRed).

storyboard.title: Formalizing the Derivative Definition
lecture_lines: Limit notation defines the exact rate.
F-prime of x equals the limit.
The distance h shrinks toward zero.
This gives the instantaneous speed here.
Like a speedometer reading right now.
animations: Display the difference quotient: f(x+h) - f(x) / h in #FFFFFF (White).
Show the limit operator lim h->0 appearing before the quotient.
Highlight the resulting derivative symbol f'(x) in #32CD32 (LimeGreen).

storyboard.title: Application: Predicting Change
lecture_lines: Derivatives tell us if we grow.
Slopes reveal peaks and valleys instantly.
We predict change at any moment.
animations: Show a moving car simulation with a position graph.
Display the instantaneous velocity as the derivative of position.
Animate the tangent line slope changing as the position graph evolves.

storyboard.title: Summary and Conclusion
lecture_lines: The derivative is the tangent slope.
It measures change at one instant.
Calculus is the math of now.
animations: Fade in a summary list of the key steps covered.
Highlight the core concept: Derivative as instantaneous rate of change.
Show a final transition screen with 'Calculus Awaits' in #FFFFFF (White).
